role: Street lighting fault controller in a local highway authority's lighting team, reviewing one fault report at a time to decide dispatch and closure
setting: A council lighting contract receives fault reports on street lights from the public, police, night scouts and a central management system (CMS) that monitors individual lantern nodes. Each record pulls together the incoming report, the asset register entry, the latest CMS reading, the unit's job history, the current job card and any supply network information from the distribution network operator. The controller must judge whether the fault sits on the electricity supply or the unit, whether this is a repeat failure after a recent repair, what to do next, and how far the current job has progressed. Signals are spread across sections and must be cross-checked: dates against dates, CMS state against the report, neighbouring outages against the network log.

supply_side_fault.instructions: Evidence places the fault on the electricity supply, not the unit.

criteria.true: Network incident logged, or three or more adjacent units dark.
criteria.false: Single unit affected, or supply evidence missing or contradicted.

repeat_failure.instructions: This unit failed again within 84 days of a completed repair.

criteria.true: Completed repair dated within 84 days before this report.
criteria.false: No completed repair in window, or completion unconfirmed.

next_action.instructions: What should the controller do next with this fault report?

criteria.close_report: Unit confirmed burning, or an open job already covers it.
criteria.hold_verify: One confirmation, such as CMS reading or scout visit, needed first.
criteria.routine_repair: Confirmed fault, no live hazard; dispatch within standard window.
criteria.urgent_make_safe: Hazard not yet made safe, or critical site dark; attend within hours.

source_support.instructions: How many independent sources confirm the information in this record?
criteria: No independent source confirms the information
Exactly one independent source confirms it
Two or three independent sources confirm it
Four or more independent sources confirm it

repair_progress.instructions: How far has work progressed toward a verified repair of this fault?
criteria: No crew visit logged against this fault
Crew attended, fault still present or unresolved
Fix recorded on site, no CMS or scout confirmation
Fix recorded and confirmed by CMS or later scout

factors.name: dark_unit_count
factors.description: Number of units on the same feeder or street currently dark, shown via supply.feeder_units_dark and the length of report.units_reported; 2 is a deliberate boundary for the supply-side claim

factors.name: dno_incident_logged
factors.description: Whether the distribution network operator has an open incident reference for the area covering the unit

factors.name: cms_state
factors.description: Latest CMS reading for the unit's node, or the whole cms section null when the unit has no node fitted

factors.name: days_since_last_repair
factors.description: Days between the completion date of the most recent prior repair in history and report.received_at; values near 84 are common to create boundary cases

factors.name: last_repair_state
factors.description: State of the most recent prior job in history: fully completed, attended but never closed, or no prior job on record

factors.name: hazard_observed
factors.description: Physical hazard noted on the current job card or report fault code: none, column door missing, column knocked down or leaning, or cable exposed

factors.name: hazard_made_safe
factors.description: Mitigation: a crew, police or the network operator has already isolated supply or fitted a temporary cover, shown by job.made_safe and job.isolated_at

factors.name: site_category
factors.description: Location type recorded in the asset register; junctions, crossings and underpasses raise the importance of a dark unit, residential side roads lower it

factors.name: planned_works_active
factors.description: Mitigation: a scheduled lantern replacement or column test window covering the report date, which can explain a dark unit without a fault

factors.name: current_job_stage
factors.description: Progress of the current job: none raised or not attended, attended but unresolved, rectified with no confirmation, rectified and confirmed by later CMS burning or a scout pass

factors.name: dates_out_of_order
factors.description: Whether a job date is inconsistent, such as completed_at earlier than attended_at or attended_at earlier than report.received_at, undermining a claimed repair

factors.name: duplicate_of_open_job
factors.description: Whether job.linked_job_ref points to an already open job on the same unit raised before this report

factors.name: report_source
factors.description: Origin of the report; police and scout reports are trusted, public web reports sometimes give the wrong unit number

sections.name: report
sections.description: Incoming fault: ref, received_at, source, fault_code, units_reported list.

sections.name: asset
sections.description: Register entry: unit_id, column_type, lantern_type, site_category, install_year, planned_works.

sections.name: cms
sections.description: Latest node reading: node_id, status_code, last_comms_at, lamp_hours; null if no node.

sections.name: history
sections.description: List of prior jobs with job_ref, raised, attended, completed, outcome_code.

sections.name: job
sections.description: Current job card: job_ref, stage, attended_at, completed_at, hazard_code, made_safe, isolated_at, linked_job_ref.

sections.name: supply
sections.description: Network information: dno_incident_ref, dno_status, feeder_units_dark, feeder_id.

rendering_notes: dark_unit_count appears as supply.feeder_units_dark (integer) and loosely as the number of ids in report.units_reported; public_web reports may list extra unit ids that cms shows burning (decoy). dno_incident_logged sets supply.dno_incident_ref to a reference string with dno_status 'open', otherwise null. cms_state maps to cms.status_code ('LF', 'OK', 'NC') with last_comms_at stale for no_comms; section_null makes the whole cms value null. days_since_last_repair and last_repair_state are rendered only as dates in history entries: completed jobs have a completed date, attended_not_completed has completed null, no_record gives an empty list; the controller must compute the gap to report.received_at. hazard_observed appears as job.hazard_code and/or report.fault_code ('DOOR', 'KNOCK', 'CABLE', or null); hazard_made_safe as job.made_safe boolean plus isolated_at timestamp, present with the same hazard about half the time. site_category is asset.site_category. planned_works_active fills asset.planned_works with window_start, window_end and work_type covering the report date, otherwise null. current_job_stage is shown through job.stage code ('RAISED', 'ATT', 'RECT') with attended_at/completed_at, and confirmation only via a cms OK reading after completed_at or a later scout entry in history; a RECT stage with cms null or NC is unconfirmed. dates_out_of_order inserts an impossible date sequence in job or the latest history entry. duplicate_of_open_job fills job.linked_job_ref with a ref matching an open history entry. report_source is report.source. Decoys: cms.lamp_hours high on healthy units, old install_year, alarming fault_code on reports where cms shows OK, feeder_units_dark of 2 without a network incident. No field may state a verdict: no 'supply_fault', 'repeat', 'priority', 'recommended_action' or 'progress' field; the answers must be inferred by comparing dates, codes and counts across sections. No free-text note fields.
